title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed sheet from a Bourbaki congress report, 'Tribu n° 59', page headed 'SYSTÈMES de RACINES (6)'. It is a draft or commentary for Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. VI §1, and it has been filed among the Hodge/motives notes.

Setting: R is a (reduced, finite) root system in a Euclidean space V. P ⊂ R is a closed subset (x, y ∈ P and x+y ∈ R imply x+y ∈ P). The goal ('la proposition') is that a closed P satisfying a condition (2) is contained in a system of positive roots. Condition (2) is not visible here; from the argument it is the condition that no nonempty sum of elements of P is 0, which follows from P ∩ (−P) = ∅ plus closedness. This is essentially Bourbaki Lie VI §1 no.7 Prop. 22.

End of step 3: one shows there is z ≠ 0 with (z, x) ≥ 0 for all x ∈ P. The page shows the last part of a contradiction argument. Under the contrary hypothesis one can build, for every n, x_1, …, x_n ∈ P with all partial sums y_i = x_1 + … + x_i in P. If n > Card P, pigeonhole gives y_i = y_j with i < j. Then x_{i+1} + … + x_j = 0, contradicting (2).

Step 4: by cor. 2 of Prop. 14, it suffices to find a basis of V whose lexicographic order makes every element of P positive. Induction on ℓ = dim V; the case ℓ = 1 comes from (1).
- Take z as in step 3, W = z^⊥, and V' = span(R ∩ W).
- R ∩ W is a root system in V': reflections s_α with α ∈ W preserve W.
- P ∩ W is closed in R ∩ W and still satisfies (2).
- Induction gives a basis (f_i) of V' making P ∩ W lexicographically positive.
- Take e_1 = z, e_{i+1} = f_i, and complete with a basis of the orthogonal complement of V' in W.
- For x ∈ P \ W, the first coordinate is (z,x)/(z,z) > 0. For x ∈ P ∩ W, the first coordinate is 0, and positivity comes from the f-coordinates.

Then a short report on no. 7 (highest root; 'the present Congress says nothing about it').

No. 8 ('pouahs et copouahs', a pun on poids/copoids, i.e. weights and coweights) fixes notation:
- Q(R) is the root lattice ('pois radiciels' = radical weights, punning on poids).
- Q(R*) is the coroot lattice.
- P(R) is the lattice dual to Q(R*), the weight lattice ('poix'); likewise P(R*).
- The text asks to state the inclusions Q(R) ⊂ P(R), etc.

Nothing here bears on the motives/Hodge material on the neighbouring pages. It is a stray Bourbaki document.
errors: Typo in original: 'i = 1, …, e'' and 'j > e' + 1' should read ℓ' (= dim V') instead of e'.

Minor gap: the claim that every element of P \ W has (z,x) > 0 relies on (z,x) ≥ 0 together with x ∉ W. This is fine, but the reader must note that the first lexicographic coordinate equals (z,x)/(z,z) because z ⊥ W. It is stated as 'clair'.

Conditions (1) and (2) and the rest of step 3 are on the previous Bourbaki page, which is absent from this folder. The argument cannot be fully checked from this page alone, but it matches the standard proof.

ideas.what: Closed subset P of a root system with P ∩ −P = ∅ (no zero sums) lies in a positive system; proof via a separating vector z and induction with lexicographic orders.
ideas.modern_name: Bourbaki Lie VI §1.7 Prop. 22 (closed symmetric-free subsets contained in positive systems)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. VI

ideas.what: Notation for root lattice Q(R), coroot lattice Q(R*), weight lattice P(R) as dual of Q(R*), with punning names (pois radiciels, poix, pouahs/copouahs).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki congress report (Tribu 59) on standard root-system material, misfiled among the motives notes. The content is routine and published in Bourbaki Lie VI. The only curiosity is archival: its presence in cote 18, possibly tied to Grothendieck's interest in reductive groups and motivic Galois groups.
transcription_corrections: In the original typescript the index is literally 'e'' (typo for ℓ'); the transcription correctly reproduces it, but it should be read as ℓ'.
The heading of no. 8 appears to read '(pouahs et copouahs)' with a slightly overstruck 'u'. It is a pun on 'poids/copoids', not a transcription error.
The handwritten '23' at the bottom left is the archive page number.
